description: CPT and HCPCS codes used in AegisHealth-KG prototype scenarios. CPT codes are copyrighted by the American Medical Association. This reference contains synthetic descriptions for educational/prototype purposes only.

codes.short_description: Continuous Glucose Monitoring — interpretation and report
codes.long_description: Ambulatory continuous glucose monitoring of interstitial tissue fluid via a subcutaneous sensor for a minimum of 72 hours; analysis, interpretation, and report by a physician or other qualified health care professional
codes.subcategory: Non-Face-to-Face Nonphysician Services — Continuous Glucose Monitoring
common_diagnosis_codes: E11.9 — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus without complications
E11.65 — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with hyperglycemia
E10.9 — Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus without complications

related_codes.description: CGM — patient-provided equipment, sensor placement, hookup, calibration, training
CGM — physician/QHP provided equipment, sensor placement, hookup, calibration, recording

codes.clinical_context: CGM provides continuous measurement of glucose levels in interstitial fluid. Code 95251 covers the physician's analysis and interpretation of the CGM data, including trend analysis, time-in-range calculations, and clinical recommendations. Typically used after a 72-hour or longer monitoring period.

codes.short_description: MRI, lower extremity joint, without contrast
codes.long_description: Magnetic resonance imaging, any joint of lower extremity; without contrast material(s)
common_diagnosis_codes: M23.21 — Derangement of medial meniscus, right knee
M76.891 — Other enthesopathy of right lower limb

related_codes.description: MRI, lower extremity other than joint; without contrast
MRI, lower extremity other than joint; without contrast then with contrast
MRI, any joint of lower extremity; without contrast then with contrast
MRI, any joint of lower extremity; with contrast

codes.clinical_context: Non-contrast MRI of lower extremity joints is the standard initial imaging modality for evaluating internal derangement (meniscal tears, ligament injuries, cartilage damage). Typically requested after failure of conservative therapy (physical therapy) and when clinical examination suggests structural pathology.

codes.long_description: Psychotherapy, 53 minutes or more with patient
codes.requires_prior_auth: After session 20 per calendar year (under AcmeCare policy)
common_diagnosis_codes: F33.1 — Major Depressive Disorder, recurrent, moderate
F33.0 — Major Depressive Disorder, recurrent, mild
F33.2 — Major Depressive Disorder, recurrent, severe

related_codes.description: Family psychotherapy with patient present, 50 minutes
Psychiatric diagnostic evaluation with medical services

codes.clinical_context: Code 90837 represents a standard full-length psychotherapy session (typically 60 minutes, with ≥53 minutes of face-to-face time). Common modalities include CBT, DBT, psychodynamic therapy, and interpersonal therapy. For ongoing treatment of mood and anxiety disorders, sessions are typically weekly to biweekly.

codes.short_description: Office visit, established patient, low complexity
codes.long_description: Office or other outpatient visit for the evaluation and management of an established patient, which requires a medically appropriate history and/or examination and low level of medical decision making
codes.clinical_context: Standard office visit code used for follow-up appointments. Referenced in clinical records as context for routine visits that may support the scenarios.

codes.short_description: Office visit, established patient, moderate complexity
codes.long_description: Office or other outpatient visit for the evaluation and management of an established patient, which requires a medically appropriate history and/or examination and moderate level of medical decision making
codes.clinical_context: Office visit code for moderate-complexity follow-ups. Used for the orthopedic examination in Scenario 2 and endocrinology follow-ups in Scenario 1.

codes.long_description: Therapeutic procedure, 1 or more areas, each 15 minutes; therapeutic exercises to develop strength, endurance, flexibility, and range of motion
codes.clinical_context: Standard physical therapy exercise code. Referenced in Scenario 2's physical therapy records as part of the conservative therapy trial required before MRI authorization.

codes.long_description: Manual therapy techniques (e.g., mobilization/manipulation, manual lymphatic drainage, manual traction), 1 or more regions, each 15 minutes
codes.clinical_context: Manual therapy code used alongside therapeutic exercises in physical therapy. Referenced in Scenario 2's conservative therapy documentation.

carc_codes.description: This (these) diagnosis(es) is (are) not covered, missing, or are invalid
carc_codes.usage_context: Used when the payer denies a claim because the diagnosis code does not support coverage for the billed service under the applicable policy. In AegisHealth-KG, mapped to mock denial category STEP_THERAPY_NOT_SATISFIED.
Used when the required prior authorization was not obtained before the service was rendered. In AegisHealth-KG, mapped to mock denial category PRIOR_AUTH_MISSING.

carc_codes.description: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer
carc_codes.usage_context: Used when the payer determines that the billed service is not medically necessary based on clinical review. In AegisHealth-KG, mapped to mock denial category MEDICAL_NECESSITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED.
